claims.text: In 2021-2025, age-standardised cancer mortality in City of Helsinki was 1.0% above the national level (ratio 1.01, 95% interval 0.986-1.034), about 12.8 more deaths a year than its age structure predicts.
Proportion of women invited to breast cancer screening (mammography) who attended, %: City of Helsinki is at 73.37 (three-year mean to 2024) against 81.6 nationally and a target of 80.
Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: City of Helsinki is at 70.97 (three-year mean to 2024) against 73.4 nationally and a target of 80.
Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: City of Helsinki is at 70.83 (three-year mean to 2024) against 73.5 nationally and a target of 80.

Waiting time for elective outpatient medical visit (physician) in primary health care exceeds 7 days from assessment of the need for treatment, % appointments kept: City of Helsinki is at 69.67 (three-year mean to 2025) against 54.7 nationally.

Waiting time of over 3 months since assessment of the need for treatment for a non-emergency appointment with a primary health care doctor in outpatient care, % of completed appointments: City of Helsinki is at 3.63 (three-year mean to 2025) against 1.7 nationally.
Among the stages that public data can measure, the earliest one where City of Helsinki is clearly worse than the country is early detection (screening participation).

Time from referral to diagnosis and from diagnosis to first treatment is not published by county for any cancer, so the Goal 3 indicator "patients access treatment within the established target times" cannot be checked from open data.

Proportion of invited to colorectal cancer screening who attended, %: 70.8% against the 80% target. Reminder and multilingual re-invitation for colorectal screening is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 33% of the gap.

Proportion of women invited to cervical cancer screening (smear test) who attended, %: 71.0% against the 80% target. HPV self-sampling kits for cervical screening non-attenders is expected to add 1.5-4.5 percentage points, closing about 33% of the gap.
First step for every county: Add first contact, referral, diagnosis and first treatment dates, plus entry route, to the national cancer quality register and publish county-level medians quarterly.
